docs.purpose: Returns the full list of jobs a tradesperson has bookmarked to track, sorted into act-now, coming-up-soon and later groups, and automatically hides jobs whose construction has already moved past the phase that trade cares about.
docs.data_story: It reads 5 tables — `lead_views`, `permits`, `trade_forecasts`, `user_profiles` and `entitlements` and writes nothing. Its response is an explicit pick-by-name projection of 10 fields, so a column added to a table upstream does not leak into the client by accident. It is called from 1 place: `mobile/src/hooks/useFlightBoard.ts`.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `QUERY`. It declares its `database.reads[]` with named columns, its response projection as an explicit whitelist, its auth class, its rate bucket and its staleness — and `outputs.writes` is forced to `"none"`. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

notes: The auto-archive filtering (dropping permits whose lifecycle-phase index has passed the selected trade's work-phase index) happens in application code after the SQL returns, not in SQL. user_profiles/entitlements come from the shared getCurrentUserContext auth helper. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: AUTH CLASS: 'authenticated' (route-guard.ts:124 + :165-167), and additionally SELF-SCOPED — `lv.user_id = $1` at :65 means an authenticated caller sees only their own saved rows. Of the seven routes in this batch this is the narrowest disclosure surface: address (street_num + street_name only, composed at :49), lifecycle state, forecast days and predicted_start. NO cost, NO income, NO contact data. // DUPLICATED CONSTANT: PHASE_INDEX is re-declared here at :21-27 with a comment at :20 saying it 'must stay in sync' with get-lead-feed.ts:821-827 — a hand-maintained duplicate with no lock; the identical table is declared a THIRD time in src/app/api/leads/flight-board/detail/[id]/route.ts is NOT present (that file imports computeTemporalGroup instead but does NOT re-declare PHASE_INDEX and does NOT auto-archive — see that route's notes). // The 999 fallback at :98 makes an unmapped trade fail OPEN (no archiving) rather than closed; it is silent. // ctx.uid is bound raw at :93 with no isUuid() normalization, unlike src/app/api/leads/detail/[id]/route.ts:66 and src/features/leads/lib/get-lead-feed.ts:1027 — an asymmetry across the three routes that read lead_views.user_id. // No LIMIT on the query (:45-69). // CENSUS: census_reads = [lead_views, permits, trade_forecasts, user_profiles, entitlements] — all five VERIFIED (user_profiles + entitlements via get-user-context.ts:99-101). Census listed no writes; the dev-mode user_profiles INSERT (get-user-context.ts:83-89) is one. | Caching: none observed — no Cache-Control, revalidate or dynamic export in the file. | Entitlement posture: READ but NOT ENFORCED — entitlements is joined at src/lib/auth/get-user-context.ts:99-100 (src/lib/entitlements/index.ts:68) but this route never reads ctx.subscription_status. | Other guards / classification: Trade-membership check at :88-90 (403). Row-level authorization is the WHERE clause itself: `lv.user_id = $1 AND lv.saved = true AND lv.lead_type = 'permit'` at :65-67 with $1 = ctx.uid (:93), so a user can only ever see their own saved rows. NOTE: ctx.uid is passed RAW here — there is no isUuid() normalization as on the detail route (contrast src/app/api/leads/detail/[id]/route.ts:66); `lv.user_id = $1` against a uuid column would throw 22P02 for a non-uuid sentinel, surfacing as the 500 at :133. | Locking tests: src/tests/db/flight-board-roundtrip.db.test.ts, src/tests/flight-board.infra.test.ts.
